instructions: The marks are indicated in the right-hand margin.
There are NINE questions in this paper.

questions.text: Choose the correct answer from the following (any seven):

subQuestions.text: The moment axis, force and the perpendicular distance in the moment of the force calculation is lying in
options: two planes perpendicular to each other
a single plane in the direction of the force
a single plane in the direction of the perpendicular distance
a single line in the direction of the force

subQuestions.text: If a force applied at any point in its line of action and is still creating the same moment about any fixed point say $P$, then the force is said to be
options: couple
sliding vector
slider couple
couple slider

subQuestions.text: The resultant force acting in the couple is
options: zero
infinite
twice the magnitude of the single force
half the magnitude of the single force

subQuestions.text: The net force of the body is zero that means the force are not being applied to the body at all and hence the body is in equilibrium.
options: The first part of the statement is false and other part is true
The first part of the statement is false and other part is false too
The first part of the statement is true and other part is false
The first part of the statement is true and other part is true too

subQuestions.text: A mass of $4\text{ kg}$ rests on a horizontal plane. The plane is gradually inclined until at an angle $\theta = 15^\circ$ with the horizontal, the mass just begins to slide. What is the coefficient of static friction between the block and the surface?
To design the trusses which of the following rules is followed?
options: All the loads are applied by the use of cables
The loads are applied at the joints
All the loads are not applied at the joints
The loads are not applied at all to the joints

subQuestions.text: The centre of gravity is the ratio of
options: the product of centroid and weight to the total weight
the addition of centroid and weight to the total weight
the subtraction of centroid and weight to the total weight
the product of centroid and weight to the total mass

subQuestions.text: In the equation of virtual work which of the following forces is neglected?
options: Reaction of any smooth surface with which the body is in contact
Reaction of a rough surface of a body which rolls on it without slipping
Reaction at a point or an axis, fixed in space, around which a body is constrained to turn
All of the above

subQuestions.text: In elastic collisions
options: only the total momentum of the colliding objects is conserved
only the total kinetic energy is conserved
both the momentum and total kinetic energy are conserved
neither momentum of the colliding bodies nor the total kinetic energy are recoverable

subQuestions.text: D'Alembert's principle is used for
options: reducing the problem of kinetics to equivalent statics problem
determining stresses in the truss
stability of floating bodies
designing safe structures

subQuestions.text: Show that the algebraic sum of the resolved part of a number of forces in a given direction, is equal to the resolved part of their resultant in the same direction.
The $30\text{ N}$ force $P$ is applied perpendicular to the portion $BC$ of the bent bar Fig. 1. Determine the moment of $P$ about point $B$ and about point $A$.

A string $ABCD$, attached to fixed points $A$ and $D$ has two equal weights of $1000\text{ N}$ attached to it at $B$ and $C$. The weights rest with the portions $AB$ and $CD$ inclined at angles as shown in Fig. 2. Find the tensions in the portions $AB$, $BC$ and $CD$ of the string, if the inclination of the portion $BC$ with the vertical is $120^\circ$.
Enunciate any two principles of equilibrium.
State and prove Lami's theorem.
Define the terms 'centre of gravity'. How would you find out the centre of gravity of a section, with a cut out hole?
Find the moment of inertia of the lamina with a circular hole of $30\text{ mm}$ diameter about the axis $AB$ as shown in Fig. 3.

A load of $1.5\text{ kN}$, resting on an inclined rough plane, can be moved up the plane by a force of $2\text{ kN}$ applied horizontally or by a force $1.25\text{ kN}$ applied parallel to the plane. Find the inclination of the plane and the coefficient of friction.
What is the difference between angle of friction and angle of repose?

A load of $2.5\text{ kN}$ is to be raised by a screw jack with mean diameter of $75\text{ mm}$ and pitch of $12\text{ mm}$. Find the efficiency of the screw jack; if the coefficient of friction between the screw and nut is $0.075$.
A truss of $5\text{ m}$ span and $2.5\text{ m}$ height is subjected to wind load as shown in Fig. 4. Find the reactions at the two supports $A$ and $E$.
A simply supported beam $AB$ of span $5\text{ m}$ is loaded as shown in Fig. 5. Find the reactions at $A$ and $B$.
State the principle of virtual work.

A simply supported beam $AB$ of span $4\text{ m}$ is subjected to a point load of $10\text{ kN}$ at a distance of $1.5\text{ m}$ from $A$. Using the principle of virtual work, determine the reactions at the two supports.

A stone is dropped from the top of a tower $50\text{ m}$ high. At the same time, another stone is thrown upwards from the foot of the tower with a velocity of $25\text{ m/s}$. When and where the two stones cross each other?
Explain the dynamic equilibrium of a rigid body in plane motion.

Two bodies of masses $45\text{ kg}$ and $30\text{ kg}$ are hung to the ends of a rope, passing over a frictionless pulley. With what acceleration the heavier mass comes down? What is the tension in the string?

A truck of mass $1.5\text{ tonnes}$ is running at a speed of $54\text{ km}$ per hour. Find its kinetic energy. If the resistance to the motion is $100\text{ N}$, find how far the truck will run before it stops.
What is meant by centre of oscillation? Describe its importance.

A spiral spring hung up at one end, and carrying a mass of $7\text{ kg}$ at the other is made to vibrate. Find the period of oscillation, if the spring is found to extend $10\text{ mm}$ for each $0.5\text{ kg}$ of mass.
What is a compound pendulum? Derive an expression for the time period of a compound pendulum.
